organizations.What they build: Industrial arms, collaborative CRX robots, CNC automation and ROBOGUIDE robot simulation. The current product page includes 2024-2026 controller and physical-AI updates.
organizations.Warm contact path: FANUC France contact page lists Lisses, Marnaz, Rennes and Les Echets; approach the Lisses team or FANUC Academy through the public form. No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: MOTOMAN industrial robots, HC collaborative arms, servo motors and automation systems. Cobots support hand-guided teaching; this is not the same as learned imitation policies.
organizations.Warm contact path: Yaskawa Europe public robotics contact and local-contact finder; the global site also lists France. No personal introduction known.

organizations.What they build: aibo companion robots combine sensing, expressive motion and cloud-supported behavior. A developer program is linked from the live aibo site; this does not make the robot open hardware.
Honda Robotics researches avatar robots and UNI-ONE mobility assistance. Its official strategy explicitly moves beyond a single general-purpose ASIMO-style humanoid toward task-specific assistance.

Japan-based Toyota develops the Human Support Robot (HSR), a mobile arm for domestic assistance. The cited 2015 developer-community program is historical, not evidence that a French student lab can borrow an HSR today. Toyota Research Institute in the US is not this row.

Develops AI chips, computing infrastructure and AI applications, with industrial-robot partners among its shareholders. Spun out Preferred Robotics; the latter now builds Kachaka products. PFR reports joint development of PLaMo-SemGround for indoor mobile-robot scene understanding in September 2026, not a verified public model release.

PFN spin-off building small autonomous mobile robots: Kachaka Pro, Kachaka Evo and the HAPiiBOT floor-cleaning robot co-developed with Amano. Publishes a Kachaka Python/ROS 2 API SDK; hardware and the full autonomy stack are not thereby open-source.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; the official Kachaka API GitHub Discussions is a public technical route, not a warm introduction.

organizations.What they build: Builds teachless robot controllers and MujinOS, combining perception, motion planning and no-code orchestration for factories and warehouses. Japan-founded business, distinct from the US subsidiary whose website supplies the cited corporate history. Its opened official news index documents a Series C in September 2023 and a $233M raise in December 2025; the Japan site independently confirms manufacturing/logistics deployments.
organizations.Warm contact path: Corporate history verifies Mujin Europe opened in Eindhoven in October 2023; approach through the official company contact, not a known personal introduction.

organizations.What they build: Develops AI-driven and remotely operated manipulation systems. Its September 2025 announcement documents TX Ghost beverage-restocking pilots at select Tokyo 7-Eleven stores; its 2026 site discusses humanoids and robot foundation-model development.

Develops collaborative picking AMRs, automated storage/retrieval systems and multi-robot control. Its live site includes customer warehouse case studies and 2024-2026 product news; performance claims are vendor claims, not independent comparisons.

Kawada group company building NEXTAGE dual-arm industrial humanoids, including NXA and Fillie, plus OPEN research variants with extensible software. Also lists HRP-2/3/4 research platforms. A humanoid upper body does not imply bipedal walking.

Japan national research institute; its humanoid group developed HRP-5P for heavy manipulation such as gypsum-board installation. The 2018 prototype is a historical research platform, not evidence of a current commercial offering.

University robotics laboratory researching integrated perception/action, assistive humanoids, musculoskeletal robots such as Kengoro and aerial robots. Its research index also lists open-source robot software. Classified as School to represent the university/laboratory entry together, not as a second duplicate university row.

Biennial robot exhibition at Tokyo Big Sight spanning production robots, service robots and components. The live site reports the 2025 show and says the next iREX is scheduled for early December 2027; RoboNext 2026 is a separate event.
Industry association publishing Japanese robot statistics and membership information, and linking to robot exhibitions. Its English site has quarterly statistics through July-September 2026.

Volunteer ROS community organizing developer meetings, study sessions, workshops and hackathons. Its official GitHub profile links connpass, Slack and organizer contact details; it is not the builder of ROS itself.
organizations.Warm contact path: unknown; official GitHub profile links community Slack, connpass and the public organizer email. These are cold outreach channels.

organizations.What they build: Investment holding group with documented participation in Telexistence's 2023 Series B. The same announcement distinguishes SoftBank Group as investor from SoftBank Robotics Group as a strategic business partner; no Pepper/NAO builder attribution is inferred.

robots_models.Name: FANUC CRX series
robots_models.Key specs: Collaborative industrial arm family; payload and reach depend on model.
robots_models.Why it matters: Industrial comparison point for safe deployment and hand-guided programming; not a low-cost open learning arm.

robots_models.Name: FANUC ROBOGUIDE
robots_models.Key specs: FANUC robot simulation software; official product index notes Omniverse integration in January 2026.
robots_models.Why it matters: Study offline industrial-cell programming before seeking access to hardware.

robots_models.Name: MOTOMAN HC10DTP
robots_models.Key specs: 10 kg payload and 1,379 mm maximum working range in the current European cobot table; hand-guided teaching.
robots_models.Why it matters: Useful industrial baseline; safety depends on the complete application and risk assessment.

robots_models.Name: MOTOMAN HC20DTP
robots_models.Key specs: 6 axes, 20 kg payload, maximum reach 1,900 mm; European page describes palletizing applications.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows how industrial collaborative handling differs from small research arms.

robots_models.Name: aibo ERS-1000
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial robot plus cloud plan; current price and French availability unknown
robots_models.Key specs: 22 actuated axes via ultracompact 1- and 2-axis actuators; OLED eyes; fish-eye cameras with SLAM; deep-learning sound/image sensing (2017 launch release). Weight not confirmed in opened sources.
robots_models.Why it matters: A consumer HRI reference, not an open locomotion research kit.

robots_models.Name: Honda Avatar Robot
robots_models.Key specs: Research avatar robot for extending human presence and physical capabilities; detailed specification unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Teleoperation is relevant to demonstration-data collection, without implying public access to Honda hardware.

robots_models.Name: Toyota Human Support Robot (HSR)
robots_models.Price / access: Research developer community; current French access unknown
robots_models.Key specs: 2015 prototype: approximately 37 kg, folding arm, 1.2 kg maximum grasped-object mass; first announced in 2012.
robots_models.Why it matters: A canonical domestic-manipulation research platform; historical Japan-focused community access must not be mistaken for an open loan offer today.

robots_models.Name: Kachaka Pro
robots_models.Key specs: Small autonomous transport robot using proprietary SLAM/navigation and deep-learning perception developed with Preferred Networks.
robots_models.Why it matters: Potential SDK-level mobile-robot experiments, subject to hardware availability; open API does not mean open hardware.

robots_models.Name: Kachaka Evo
robots_models.Key specs: 100 kg-payload AMR; official company site announces formal sales from October 2026.
robots_models.Why it matters: Tracks expansion from small delivery robots into industrial transport, not an inexpensive student purchase.

robots_models.Name: HAPiiBOT
robots_models.Key specs: Small commercial floor-cleaning robot co-developed with Amano using AI image recognition and SLAM.
robots_models.Why it matters: An example of autonomous navigation in an operational product rather than a lab-only benchmark.

robots_models.Name: Kachaka API SDK
robots_models.Price / access: Apache-2.0 SDK; compatible robot and API terms required
robots_models.Key specs: Official Python 3.10+ and ROS 2 Humble SDK; gRPC access to movement, docking, state and sensors.
robots_models.Why it matters: Concrete software contribution surface for a Paris lab even before a broader institutional partnership.

robots_models.Name: PLaMo-SemGround
robots_models.Key specs: Indoor mobile-robot environment-understanding foundation model; joint development announced September 9, 2026 on PFR site. Architecture and public weights unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Relevant perception research lead, not evidence of a released VLA or a ready-to-use robot policy.

robots_models.Name: MujinController PickWorker
robots_models.Key specs: Teachless bulk-picking controller launched in January 2015 according to official corporate history.
robots_models.Why it matters: Highlights integrated perception and motion planning as an alternative to repeated manual waypoint teaching.

robots_models.Name: MujinOS
robots_models.Key specs: Proprietary no-code automation platform for perception, motion control and orchestration across industrial robot brands.
robots_models.Why it matters: Relevant industrial deployment architecture; not an open-source imitation-learning model.

robots_models.Name: TX Ghost
robots_models.Key specs: Beverage-restocking robot used in September 2025 pilots at select 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo; exact kinematics and payload unknown.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows real retail manipulation with a robot/service workflow; not a walking humanoid or a public research kit.

robots_models.Name: Rapyuta PA-AMR
robots_models.Key specs: Collaborative order-picking mobile robots coordinated with warehouse workers and multi-robot controls.
robots_models.Why it matters: A multi-robot coordination case study with deployed warehouse workflows.

robots_models.Name: NEXTAGE (NXA)
robots_models.Key specs: Dual-arm industrial humanoid upper-body platform; NXA released in 2018 with increased payload and speed over NX01C. OPEN research variant also offered.
robots_models.Why it matters: Research-friendly dual-arm manipulation direction, but not an affordable bipedal platform.

robots_models.Name: NEXTAGE Fillie
robots_models.Key specs: Compact NEXTAGE variant released in 2022; Fillie OPEN research version is ROS-compatible.
robots_models.Why it matters: Useful reference for two-arm experiments through a lab that already owns the hardware.

robots_models.Name: HRP-5P
robots_models.Key specs: 2018 research prototype: 182 cm, 101 kg, 37 degrees of freedom; demonstrated autonomous gypsum-board installation.
robots_models.Why it matters: Historical whole-body manipulation benchmark, not a commercial humanoid purchase recommendation.

robots_models.Name: Kengoro
robots_models.Key specs: Human-mimetic musculoskeletal humanoid with tendon-driven structures; 2016 papers describe artificial perspiration for cooling.
robots_models.Why it matters: A mechanics-heavy research contrast to software-first low-cost learning; paper reproduction is more realistic than hardware replication.

summary: Who leads: FANUC and Yaskawa anchor industrial automation; Toyota, Honda, Sony, AIST and University of Tokyo JSK contribute assistive, consumer and humanoid research. This is a curated top-15-scale map, not a market-share ranking.

Where money is: commercial automation targets factories, warehouses and retail; Telexistence documented a $170M Series B in 2023 with SoftBank Group participation, while Mujin lists a $233M raise in December 2025. Other startup round labels remain unknown where primary evidence was not established.

Where demand is: logistics picking and transport, industrial manipulation, beverage restocking and human assistance recur in opened primary sources; deployment engineering matters as much as model capability.

Gap/opportunity: industrial and humanoid hardware is generally proprietary and inaccessible to a small Paris lab; test the low-cost robot-learning hypothesis through reproducible software, not by assuming Japanese hardware sponsorship.

Best entry point: approach FANUC France, Yaskawa Europe or Mujin Europe for a technical talk or supervised demo; contribute to the Kachaka SDK or exchange ROS 2 tutorials with ROS Japan before seeking a larger partnership.
